channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Anthropic Expands Into Finance With Claude Tool Linking Advisors to Analytics
item.description: Anthropic PBC is pitching financial advisers on a version of Claude that blends the chatbot with financial analytics and risk management technology run by BlackRock Inc., Vanguard Group Inc. and other firms.
item.dc:creator: Tanya Falenczyk and Silla Brush

item.title: Waymo Expands Paid Robotaxi Service to Las Vegas, Its 15th City
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Waymo is now serving paying customers in Las Vegas, marking the 15th US city where it offers hailable robotaxis.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung

item.title: Rig at Miami Construction Site Falls, Injuring Several
item.description: A rig collapsed in Miami’s financial district at the construction site of Citadel’s new headquarters, crushing several cars and snarling traffic. Videos and pictures provided by Miami Fire Rescue showed three cars impacted by the metal structure with a white BMW SUV still smoldering after a fire was put out on Brickell Bay Drive. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stocks Fall on AI Fears as 10-Year Yield Hits 5%
item.description: A rout in chipmakers dragged down stocks as leaders of artificial-intelligence giants called for a development slowdown, with the market also hit by a rally in oil that lifted Treasury 10-year yields to 5%. Lori Calvasina, Head of US Equity Strategy at RBC Capital Markets, gives her equity call amid the chip rout and energy price concerns. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump ataca a CEO de Anthropic por llamado a ralentizar la IA
item.description: El presidente Donald Trump arremetió contra el director ejecutivo de Anthropic PBC, Dario Amodei, por pedir que se desacelere el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial, intensificando su oposición a la implantación de nuevas medidas de control para esta tecnología.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: Barclays CEO on Bonds, AI, UK Taxing Banks
item.description: Barclays Plc Chief Executive Officer CS Venkatakrishnan discusses why the bond market is under pressure, how the bank is using artificial intelligence and he called on the UK government to not raise taxes on banks in the next budget. He speaks to Bloomberg's Dani Burger (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Musk’s xAI Resolves Claims Against Apple Over AI Competition
item.description: Elon Musk’s xAI and X Corp. said they resolved an antitrust lawsuit against Apple Inc. that accused the iPhone maker of favoring OpenAI’s ChatGPT over other chatbot makers.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: Why the AI Sell-Off Is a Buying Opportunity: Tengler
item.description: AI stocks are under pressure as fresh safety warnings revive fears that the trade has run too far. Is the AI boom cracking, or is this the dip investors have been waiting for? Nancy Tengler, Laffer Tengler CEO and CIO, says the latest sell-off is more “hiccup” than collapse. She argues the AI buildout is still a once-in-a-generation opportunity. She breaks down where the winners could emerge and when to start buying. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Tariffs Face a Canada Test
item.description: Canada is pushing back against President Trump’s tariff strategy, but without shutting the door on negotiations. PIIE’s Mary Lovely explains why Mark Carney may have found the limits of US trade leverage and warns that America’s closest partners could increasingly diversify away from the U.S. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What Blockchain Still Needs to Win Wall Street
item.description: Kaiko CEO Ambre Soubiran joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why blockchain adoption on Wall Street is taking longer than expected. She argues the technology is ready, but tokenized markets still need trusted data, risk controls and traditional market safeguards before 24/7 trading and instant settlement can scale. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ex-Google DeepMind Insider: Why We MUST Slow Down AI Now
item.description: Alex Turner, a former Google DeepMind research scientist, joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why he left the firm over safety concerns and why he thinks AI progress is moving too fast for governments, companies, and even superpowers like the US and China to control. He reveals how tracking compute could be the key to real regulation, and why Big Tech’s calls to “slow down” might be both sincere and a power play. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Canada’s Carney on Capital Investment, AI, US Trade
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney talks about efforts to increase foreign investment in the nation, seeking coordination on artificial intelligence safety, and the state of trade with the United States. He joins Bloomberg News' Ottawa Bureau Chief Brian Platt ahead of the country's first national investment summit in Toronto. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Bosses Risk Clash With Wall Street Over Safety
item.description: Anthropic PBC and OpenAI will have to weigh their calls to tap the brakes on artificial intelligence development against forces in the tech industry, financial markets and the Trump administration. Parmy Olson, Bloomberg Opinion tech columnist, discusses the impact of recent calls from big tech bosses to rein in the pursuit of cutting-edge AI models. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Attacks Anthropic CEO Over Call to Slow AI Development
item.description: President Donald Trump attacked Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei for urging a slowdown in artificial intelligence development, intensifying his opposition to new guardrails for the technology.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: US Data Centers Set to Burn More Natural Gas Than Most Nations
item.description: Data centers in the United States will consume more natural gas than most countries within a decade, according to a new outlook from BloombergNEF.
item.dc:creator: Julian Hast

item.title: Some AI Players Are Worse Than Others, Amodei Says
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei talks about the need for oversight when it comes to developing artificial intelligence. He spoke to Bloomberg's Emily Chang on "The Circuit" in June. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Microsoft Joins Rivals Calling for Caution With AI Models
item.description: Microsoft Corp.’s artificial intelligence researchers have released a new set of guiding tenets that place limits on the company’s development of cutting-edge AI models.
item.dc:creator: Matt Day

item.title: Dangote Refinery IPO Rush Crashes Some Nigerian Trading Apps
item.description: Demand for shares in Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE overwhelmed some of the many Nigerian investing apps soon after an initial public offering opened Monday.
item.dc:creator: Yinka Ibukun and Emele Onu

item.title: Chevron Australia President on LNG outlook
item.description:
Balaji Krishnamurthy, President of Chevron in Australia, discusses the outlook for LNG supply and demand, and pricing levels, as energy disruptions continue on Middle East tensions. He speaks with Haslinda Amin, on the sidelines of Gastech in Bangkok, on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade".
Correct: video has been edited to fix the spelling of Bangkok in a segment. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Bosses Clash With Trump on Their Calls to Slow AI Development
item.description: AI developers including Anthropic PBC and OpenAI are clashing with the Trump administration over their calls for an industrywide slowdown in artificial intelligence development, a proposal that’s already triggered a selloff across technology stocks and has brought into question the resilience of a global data center boom.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Frier and Michael Shepard
